project.name: Kurrajong Apartments balcony waterproofing, 41 Kurrajong Parade
project.summary: The owners corporation of a fully occupied 6-storey, 42-unit Class 2 strata building in Hurstville, constructed in 2008 and out of warranty, renews the waterproofing of all 42 leaking balconies and of the ground-floor courtyard podium over the basement car park, like for like. A remedial building consultant leads, with structural, landscape and hydraulic consultants, and tenders one AS 4000 lump sum contract; the works are exempt from consent.

documents.content: The remedial building consultant's report after visual inspection, leak mapping, flood tests and opening-up at four representative balconies. Sections: ## Building description (existing building constructed in 2008, Class 2 with a Class 7a basement car park, rise in storeys 6, 42 apartments, a single-level basement car park below a ground-floor communal courtyard podium with planter boxes, pitched metal roof outside the scope), ## Findings (water is entering the basement car park beneath the ground-floor communal courtyard; the podium pavers sit on pedestals over a membrane installed in 2008; podium flood test at the courtyard outlets; membrane stops short of the door sills though set-down is adequate at all thresholds and door frames are retained; reversed falls; outlets with no puddle flange and no overflow; balustrade posts core-drilled through the membrane; tiles bonded to the membrane; the 2019 hazardous materials survey found no asbestos in balcony build-ups; no spalling, cracking or exposed reinforcement on any balcony; no plant or services on the balconies), ## Options (A patch repair, B full renewal of the balconies and the courtyard podium like for like, recommended), ## Recommended budget (a construction budget of $1,960,000 ex GST for Option B, of which about $280,000 is the podium), ## Approvals (exempt; DBP Act applies; not a heritage item), ## Warranty (the building is out of warranty and no claim is being pursued), ## Next steps (all work from within the balconies, no external access equipment; one continuous stage).
